articles.title: Does Trump’s 60-day tariff waiver really give relief to India? What it means for US trade deal & oil prices
articles.summary: What does US President Donald Trump’s decision to waive sanctions on Russia and tariffs on countries buying oil from Moscow really mean for India?
articles.body: What does US President Donald Trump’s decision to waive sanctions on Russia and tariffs on countries buying oil from Moscow really mean for India? The US decision to waive the proposed sanctions under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 is clearly aimed at securing relief for its own country.The development comes amid America’s shifting approach to Russian energy. In a separate deal, Russia agreed to release more than 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel for the US and global markets, with further supplies proposed for subsequent months.While the US-Russia diesel deal primarily focused on the bilateral US-Russia relations, the tariff waiver is mostly directed to India and China. The threatened 100% tariffs on the five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas were due to take effect 30 days after the legislation’s approval on September 18.Also Read | The return of Middle East oil: Has Iran lost control of Strait of Hormuz & why are crude prices still up?What Trump has doneTrump invoked Section 115 of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 to issue the waiver. He certified that it was in the national interest of the US."I have submitted to the Congress a certification that the issuance of such a waiver is in the national interests of the United States and a report explaining the basis for the certification, consistent with section 115(b) of the Graham Act," Trump said.The waiver applies to duties under Sections 112 and 113, which authorised tariffs of up to 500% on goods that are imported from Russia and up to 100% on goods from the five largest buyers of Russian-origin crude oil or natural gas. India and China were among the countries potentially covered by the latter provision.But, Natalia Katona, Commodity Analyst sees the move as less of a gift to Moscow than an attempt to keep a lid on oil prices.“Russian crude continued to find buyers despite the tariff threat, effectively the entire November loading programme of Russian export grades has been sold off even though it could’ve been subjected to tariffs,” she tells TOI.“Enforcing the Lindsey Graham Act would risk disrupting future Russian crude flows and pushing Brent above its current level of around $110 a barrel. With US elections approaching in early November, my reading is that Trump wants to avoid another oil-price shock at all costs,” she says.What it means for IndiaFor India, the immediate relief is for its crude supply basket and exporters. If India decided to give up Russian crude oil, its single largest supplier would have gone off the table, with no easy replacement amid Middle East tensions. If it continued to buy Russian crude, then the 100% tariffs would have weighed on its exports to the US.Russian oil supplies to India hit a record high earlier this year when the closure of Strait of Hormuz limited the Middle East crude supplies.But recently, buying patterns have made a notable shift to the Middle East as supplies through the Strait of Hormuz ease and China begins competing for the same Russian barrels, driving up the cost of oil from Moscow.Pankaj Srivastava, Senior Vice President, Commodity Market - Oil at Rystad Energy is of the view that India was strategically prepared for the Graham bill, with crude supply from the Middle East rising significantly to approximately 2.5 million bpd in September, while Russian imports declined to around 1.5 million bpd.The increase in Middle Eastern supply was supported by the continued operation of multiple logistics channels, including the Strait of Hormuz, dark fleet movements, ship-to-ship transfers, alternative Red Sea and Suez Canal routes, and the East-West Pipeline.“As a result, Middle Eastern crude exports increased to nearly 15 million barrels per day in September, strengthening India's import availability. At the same time, higher insurance and freight costs associated with Black Sea exports, following recent attacks in the region, reduced the competitiveness of Russian crude,” Pankaj Srivastava tells TOI.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();According to the expert, with ongoing refinery expansions and strong diesel crack margins supporting exports, the waiver further improves feedstock security for Indian refiners.“This development is also constructive for global distillate markets and could provide additional support to diesel and jet fuel balances in the US and Europe,” he says.In addition, Abu Dhabi National Oil Company's decision to align Murban crude pricing with Dubai Platts from 1 November is expected to enhance pricing transparency and improve procurement flexibility for Asian refiners.“Overall, the combination of the Russian waiver, increased Middle Eastern supply, the UAE's evolving position within OPEC, and the Murban pricing changes is positive for Indian refiners, strengthening their potential to increase diesel and jet fuel exports and generate economic benefits,” he adds.The caveatOne very important point that is worth noting is that this waiver is for a 60-day period. In fact, even globally despite America’s diesel supply deal with Russia and the sanctions waiver, crude oil prices continue to stay near $110 per barrel.Pankaj Srivastava says the waiver was largely anticipated and is expected to provide modest support to crude prices while easing supply-side geopolitical risks for India.As Natalia Katona points out: Removing the threat also removes a potential deterrent for competing buyers of Russian crude.“So far, purchasing patterns show little sign of changing. For instance, China had already secured November-loading ESPO cargoes by early September, ahead of its usual buying schedule. India’s purchases by mid-October point to Russian crude flows of more or less the same 1.8 million b/d unchanged from September,” she tells TOI.And, the pricing story is more complicated than the headline premium suggests.According to Katona, the Urals deliveries to India are generally priced against Dated Brent, which reflects the tight physical crude market.“Dated Brent was trading $20/bbl above ICE Brent futures for most of October and still is $10/bbl higher, therefore a cargo priced at Dated parity can still carry a substantial premium when compared to any other futures benchmark,” she explains.Urals has moved from a premium of around $8/bbl to Dated Brent a month ago to roughly Dated parity today, with a possibility for that differential to soften further.“Russian suppliers are adjusting to a higher physical benchmark and elevated freight costs to keep their barrels competitive. But a falling premium is not the same as a falling oil price,” she notes.“India may negotiate a better differential with Russian grades and will still face a higher outright bill if the benchmark itself (in this case, Dated Brent) rises. With China competing for Russian barrels and global physical supplies tightening, the waiver eases India’s tariff risk without resolving its supply problem,” she adds.But the weather may work in India’s favour over the coming months.In September-October, a total of 12 cargoes carrying Russian oil transited the Northern Sea Route, on their way to China.According to Katona, these flows should gradually halt as ice takes over most of the Arctic Ocean again, lowering the availability of Urals cargoes for China through the NSR.“Considering India is generally closer to Russia geographically (entailing a lower freight cost), from November onwards Russian sellers of grades loading in European ports (Urals, Siberian Light or Russian CPC) should have a general prevalence for Indian deliveries,” she believes.India-US trade dealThe impending trade deal with the US is yet another important aspect of this whole equation.India and the US have been negotiating a trade deal for quite some time now with varying signals coming from time to time. Recently both the US and India indicated that the first phase of the deal is close to being finalised. Yet India has stressed that a trade agreement is possible only if it manages to gain a competitive advantage to its peers.The impending tariffs of up to 100% for India’s crude purchases from Russia would have weighed on the discussions. Now, what the waiver of tariffs does is give breathing space to India.Interestingly, Rubio on Monday said that the US was "very close" to concluding a trade agreement with India, and also indicated that the decision to grant a tariff waiver for purchases of Russian oil had been linked to the ongoing trade negotiations."We're trying to finalise the trade deal with India right now. We're very close to doing that. So that's one of the things we take into consideration when the President makes a decision about national security waivers and things of that nature,” Rubio said.But, Ajay Srivastava, founder, Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) says that India should not mistake that pause for lasting protection.China already has a separate assurance against tariff increases by the US until January 10, 2027, under the Busan agreement.“Washington can continue buying Russian diesel, leave China protected and keep the threat hanging over New Delhi,” Ajay Srivastava tells TOI.“Washington has bought Russian uranium and fertilizers and is now arranging purchases of Russian diesel. It has protected China against tariff increases under a separate agreement. Demanding an Indian price for withholding Russian-oil penalties would expose the selective nature of the policy,” he warns.Yet another factor is that Trump’s policies have done little till now to inspire confidence that any relief would be permanent.“Washington could invoke another statute, another investigation or another alleged grievance. India should insist on knowing exactly which US tariffs would fall, under what legal authority and for how long,” the GTRI founder says about the trade deal negotiations.“The US is entitled to negotiate for its interests. articles.title: Trump administration announces $8 billion farm relief plan as fuel, fertilizer costs bite
articles.summary: President Donald Trump announced at a Kansas rally on Monday that his administration is offering an $8 billion aid package for farmers in the face of high diesel and fertilizer costs.
articles.body: President Donald Trump announced at a Kansas rally on Monday that his administration is offering an $8 billion aid package for farmers in the face of high diesel and fertilizer costs. The package comes just two weeks before midterm elections, where political headwinds threaten to complicate Republicans’ efforts to hold on to seats in some farm-heavy, typically red states. The war with Iran has added to pressure on America’s farmers as they prepare for the crucial harvest season: Fertilizer costs have soared this year after the Middle East conflict disrupted one-third of the world’s supply that normally flowed through the Strait of Hormuz. Farmers are also major users of diesel fuel for their farming equipment, and have seen the price of that key workhorse fuel hit record levels. It’s the the second time in 11 months that the US Department of Agriculture has offered a one-time payment to farmers. This program, which it called a “harvest fuel relief program,” is similar to a $12 billion aid package announced in December. That earlier program helped farmers who then were primarily hurt by the trade disputes sparked by the Trump administration’s tariffs, which were cutting into export demand for their crops and other products. Current polling projects close Senate races or even Democratic victories in many states that Trump easily won in the last three presidential elections, including Iowa, Kansas, Ohio and Texas. Democrats are forecast to win Senate races in North Carolina and Georgia. Kansas, which has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932, is seen as too close to call in a race between Sen. Roger Marshall and Democrat Adam Hamilton. Trump credited Marshall with helping to get the latest farm aid package in place at the rally Monday night. And he promised even more help for farmers “when the Republicans win.” “We love our farmers,” Trump told the crowd.

articles.title: US Housing Starts Fall to One of the Worst Paces Since Pandemic
articles.summary: New US residential construction declined in September to one of the weakest paces since the pandemic and building permits for single-family homes slid, highl...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- New US residential construction declined in September to one of the weakest paces since the pandemic and building permits for single-family homes slid, highlighting a languishing housing market.

Housing starts decreased 5.2% to an annualized rate of 1.22 million, a four-month low, according to federal government data released Tuesday. The pace trailed all estimates in a Bloomberg survey of economists.

Starts of single-family homes decreased to the lowest level in a year, and applications for permits on those dwellings — a gauge of future construction — dropped to the lowest since early 2023.

The residential real estate market is being constrained by affordability challenges now further compounded by higher mortgage rates. Homebuilders, whose confidence has slumped to a 14-year low, may also be reluctant to begin construction on new homes before making more progress on inventories.

The report showed new construction on multifamily projects, which include apartments and can be volatile on a monthly basis, fell nearly 7%.

Sluggish home construction has weighed on economic growth in five of the last six quarters. Before Tuesday's report, the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's GDPNow forecast penciled in residential investment declining an annualized 1.3% in the third quarter.

Completions of single-family homes last month dropped to the weakest pace in more than six years.

"Housing construction — one of the economic sectors most sensitive to interest rates — is facing intensifying headwinds as mortgage rates have moved significantly higher...With inventories already elevated and builders increasingly pessimistic about future sales, residential construction is likely to remain a drag on interest-rate-sensitive activity in coming months."

Starts of one-family homes in the South, the nation's largest homebuilding region, dropped to the lowest level since January. They also fell in the West and Midwest.

The new residential construction data are volatile, and the government report showed 90% confidence that the total monthly change ranged from a 17% decline to a 6.6% gain.

articles.title: CNN warns Trump White House: Restore Air Force One access or face further legal action
articles.summary: The White House has been excluding CNN from President Trump’s trips on Air Force One, disrupting a decades-old tradition of pooled TV coverage.
articles.body: The White House has been excluding CNN from President Donald Trump’s trips on Air Force One, disrupting a decades-old tradition of pooled TV coverage. Now an attorney for CNN is warning that the network will take additional legal action if the White House continues to prevent its news crews from covering the president. “These efforts to retaliate and discriminate against CNN based on the content of its news coverage are mistaken, counterproductive, and unlawful,” Ted Boutrous, outside counsel for CNN, wrote in a letter to the Justice Department on Monday. The demand letter stated that CNN “will be forced to pursue additional judicial relief” if the action continues. The letter is the latest extension of a legal fight that began when Trump banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House one month ago. The banned news outlets sued, alleging violations of the First and Fifth Amendments. A federal judge intervened to restore access, first temporarily and then longer-term, while the lawsuit over the ban plays out. The longer-term ruling by US District Judge Tim Kelly issued a preliminary injunction in favor of the plaintiffs, saying Trump’s ban likely violated the First Amendment because it amounted to unconstitutional viewpoint discrimination. Following the judge’s order, the Trump administration restored White House access for the banned news outlets. But the Justice Department has justified the ban in court, and the White House has sought other ways to single out journalists. Blocking CNN from traveling on Air Force One is one of those ways. The administration appears to be relying on an ongoing court case involving The Associated Press, which filed suit last year when Trump blocked AP reporters from Air Force One, the Oval Office and other areas with limited space for the press pool. Trump took action against The AP because the news wire didn’t immediately start using his new name for the Gulf of Mexico like he wanted. In June 2025, an appeals court panel partially lifted the stay obtained by The AP and stated that the news wire was not likely to succeed on the merits “because these restricted presidential spaces” like Air Force One and the Oval Office “are not First Amendment fora opened for private speech and discussion.” But the ruling was “non-binding and non-precedential,” Boutrous pointed out in his letter, so it is not binding on other cases. Boutrous also addressed the appeals panel ruling in the AP case by showing that the Oval Office and Air Force One have become the primary places “where the president interacts with the press by briefing reporters and answering questions.” In the second Trump administration, the president has fielded more than 4,700 questions in the Oval Office, aboard Air Force One and on the tarmac. By contrast, he has fielded just about 150 questions in the White House press briefing room since returning to office in January 2025. So far this year, through September, Trump has appeared in the White House briefing room only 4 times, while he has held “43 press events in the Oval Office” and answered questions aboard and around Air Force One “51 times,” Boutrous wrote. The AP is still waiting on a decision from the full appeals court. Meanwhile, some of its access has been restored. The White House has not explicitly said that it is following its AP playbook in its actions against CNN. In fact, it has provided “no written notice and offered no explanation” for excluding CNN from recent trips, Boutrous wrote in the letter. The Justice Department did not respond to a CNN reporter’s request for comment about the demand letter on Tuesday morning. But in a combative statement following the judge’s longer-term order last week, a White House official said “the Fake News has no place demanding a spot in the President’s Oval Office.” ‘Those spaces belong… to all Americans’ The five major TV networks take turns providing pooled TV coverage of the president’s events and trips, and news organizations worldwide rely on the footage for their own reports and shows. On several occasions when CNN was next in the TV pool rotation, the network was left off the White House’s list, signaling that it was “being barred from fully performing its pool duties,” Boutrous wrote. Most recently, it happened last weekend, when CNN was supposed to provide pooled coverage of the president’s trip to Georgia and Florida but was excluded from the out-of-town travel pool. In a show of solidarity, the other major networks have declined to fill in when CNN has been excluded. The demand letter noted that CNN has participated in the TV pool and covered presidents in the Oval Office and on Air Force One for 45 years. “That is because those spaces belong not to any particular president or administration but to all Americans, and CNN and other members of the press serve as surrogates for the public when covering the White House,” Boutrous wrote. The demand letter may foreshadow new legal filings in the ongoing lawsuit by CNN, MS NOW and Politico. Boutrous wrote in Monday’s letter that CNN would like the administration to “confirm in writing” that “the White House abandon any policy of excluding CNN from the Oval Office and Air Force One” and stop preventing assigned pool duties. He included a Thursday at 5 p.m. Eastern deadline. “If these actions persist,” he wrote, “CNN will have no choice but to return to the court to defend its rights, and it is prepared to fight as long as is necessary to secure them.”

articles.title: Looted French goods are popping up on resale site Vinted
articles.summary: The second-hand online marketplace Vinted has removed listings of looted French goods and stepped up checks on “suspicious” adverts, as the country’s authorities seek to prevent goods stolen during riots from being sold online.
articles.body: The second-hand online marketplace Vinted has removed listings of looted French goods and stepped up checks on “suspicious” adverts, as the country’s authorities seek to prevent goods stolen during riots from being sold online. Vinted says its teams have taken “immediate action to identify and remove listings linked to the looting,” following a weekend of unrest that saw shops ransacked across France, with the cost of property damage and theft estimated to be several hundred million dollars. “The sale of stolen goods, or soliciting them, is strictly prohibited on Vinted, and we have zero tolerance for it,” the company said in a statement, noting that it had “stepped up monitoring of suspicious listings.” Accounts found to have breached its rules could face permanent bans, Vinted said, adding that it is working with law enforcement and French authorities to “detect and counter emerging risks and malicious behaviour.” The response comes as the French government increases scrutiny of online marketplaces following reports that goods stolen during Saturday’s unrest were being offered for sale online. Serge Papin, France’s small businesses minister, said on ​X that authorities had called a meeting Monday with online marketplace operators and officials ​from the interior and justice ministries. On Tuesday, he said the government had obtained commitments from platforms to detect and remove ads for looted items, and was also monitoring sales itself, warning that anyone selling stolen goods would be tracked down and prosecuted. Major retailers including luxury groups such as Louis Vuitton and Rolex and beauty retailer Sephora were caught up in the violence, Reuters reported. Sephora said several of its stores in France had been ransacked, with employees facing “violence, fear and great tension.” In a statement posted on LinkedIn, the company’s EMEA president, Catherine Spindler, said it had decided to close all its stores at 5pm Saturday and keep its city-center locations closed the following day, for the safety of staff and customers. “The strength of a company is not its stores or its windows. It is the women and men who keep it alive,” the post reads. Luxury fashion brand Burberry also confirmed that its store on Rue Saint-Honoré in Paris was temporarily closed while it assessed the situation. The emergence of suspected looted goods on resale platforms presents another challenge for retailers already dealing with damage to their stores and disruption to their businesses. Vinted prohibits the sale of stolen goods and relies on a range of checks, including reports from retailers and users, to identify suspicious listings. Founded in Lithuania in 2008, Vinted has grown into one of Europe’s largest second-hand marketplaces. France, the UK and Italy are among its biggest markets, according to Reuters.

articles.title: Oil prices move higher as traders adjust to a new normal in the Middle East
articles.summary: Oil prices surged in early trading Tuesday, as energy markets adjusted to a new normal in the Middle East.
articles.body: Oil prices surged in early trading Tuesday, as energy markets adjusted to a new normal in the Middle East. The increase in crude prices threatened to drive up the cost of gas in the United States just two weeks before the midterm elections. U.S. crude prices jumped as much as 5% to about $109 a barrel, the highest price since April, while the price of international Brent crude climbed 1.5% to more than $111, its highest price since May. Prices pulled back later in the morning, after weaker-than-expected U.S. housing starts raised the prospect of a broader slowdown and lower demand. Prices for advanced oil contracts dated for next year also hit record highs, “implying an extended period of high oil prices deep into 2027,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note Tuesday. “The 2027 contracts are moving higher as well as the possible reality of higher for longer oil prices sink in,” Peter Boockvar, author of the Boock Report and chief investment officer of OnePoint BFG Wealth Partners, said in a note Tuesday. High gas prices have become a major issue for voters in the midterms, where Republicans face dwindling odds of maintaining their control of Congress. A recent NBC News poll found that 67% of U.S. adults believe gas prices are a “very serious” or “somewhat serious” problem. A majority also said that current economic conditions have caused them to change their spending habits. U.S. gasoline prices had started off the week lower. At $4.28 a gallon, the national average price of unleaded was on pace to reach its lowest level in a month. But that trend is likely to be upended as higher crude prices filter through to the pump. Several factors were contributing to Tuesday’s oil price hikes. The cost of chartering a large tanker vessel to transport oil through the Strait of Hormuz has quadrupled since September, data shows. Much of that increase is a risk premium, both for sailors and insurance. During the past two weeks, at least 18 ⁠vessels have been attacked in the strait, the ship-tracking group Kpler said in a note ⁠Monday. The higher cost of transport has begun to offset the recent bump in supply from a growing number of ships moving through the strait. The Iranian attacks on ships have also prompted investor speculation that the Trump administration will be more likely to escalate against Iran after the midterms, the Deutsche Bank analysts said. Iran-aligned Houthi rebels also claimed Monday that they had hit airport, energy and military targets in Saudi Arabia, as well as a ​training camp in Yemen for that government’s security forces. The U.K. will begin deploying fighter jets over Saudi Arabia to help protect against further Houthi attacks, the Defense Ministry said Tuesday. The entry of another country’s military into the regional hostilities was taken as a further sign of escalating tensions.

articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Bank of America Corp. has kicked off its second investment-grade bond sale in days, offering perpetual notes following last week's $8 billion capital raising.

The bonds would be first callable in five years, and initial price discussions involve a yield of 7.5% to 7.625%, according to a person familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified because they're not authorized to speak publicly. The company sold $2.5 billion of such notes in July 2025 at a 6.25% yield.

Bank of America brought an unusual Friday high-grade bond offering on Oct. 16, braving the market after a turbulent week in credit markets disrupted fundraising plans for numerous borrowers.

Markets are uncertain Tuesday, with a fresh round of AI-fueled worries sending stocks lower and Treasuries higher. A measure of credit risk for US investment-grade bonds rose after logging its highest close since March 31 on Monday.

The firm's shares finished yesterday at their lowest since May 15, extending a post-earnings decline as Bank of America reported that both its stock and fixed-income traders' results fell short of estimates. It also disclosed a $1.2 billion charge for fines for money laundering and sanctions violations.

Bank of America has sold $25 billion of investment-grade notes this year.

articles.title: Bank of America’s fine is a warning to Wall Street
articles.summary: What is needed is a fundamental restructuring of financial crime education in the private sector.
articles.body:
Last week’s $1.2 billion fine imposed upon Bank of America for its failures involving money laundering and sanctions evasion should act as a wake-up call for the entire financial sector. This is not just because of the enormous size of the fine levied, but because of why the bank was fined, and the fundamental weaknesses in how financial institutions approach financial crimes to begin with.

Two key failures from Bank of America stand out: the failure to adequately identify and report more than a billion dollars of suspicious activity tied to national security and other priority illicit finance risks, and the fact that 76 percent of its risk factor weights in its transaction monitoring system remained unchanged for five years between 2018 and 2023. Of the weights that did change, approximately 80 percent were actually reduced.

These findings expose a fundamental disconnect between how financial institutions approach financial crime and the broader national security and geopolitical environment in which it occurs.

For much of the financial sector, money laundering and sanctions evasion are viewed primarily in the context of operational compliance: matching patterns, examining new behaviors and running names through sanctions lists. This is predominantly treated as operational, check-the-box compliance work.

While these functions are certainly necessary to maintain an effective program to fight financial crime, focusing exclusively on compliance misses the actual reason individuals are sanctioned to begin with, and the national security risks associated with money laundering and financial crime.

Not all financial crimes are created equal. Your local drug dealer is not an equal national security risk to someone evading sanctions to support the North Korean nuclear program. But to understand this distinction, one must fundamentally alter how they approach financial crime to place it in the context of American national security, foreign policy and a rapidly shifting geopolitical environment.

Take the Iran War, for example. As it currently stands, the primary strategy through which the U.S. hopes to achieve victory is economic warfare . Stifling Iran’s ability to evade sanctions and launder funds is a core focus of the Trump administration’s strategy right now.

From the perspective of American foreign policy objectives, the strategic consequences of missing Iranian sanctions evasion can be far greater than those of missing unrelated illicit transactions involving Australian tobacco.

But as we saw with Bank of America, when one of the world’s largest banks leaves most of its risk factor weights unchanged for five years, it raises serious questions about institutional complacency in a rapidly shifting global environment.

During the years from 2018 to 2023, we saw a historic shift in illicit finance risk when Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022. Sanctions were imposed on a massive scale, Russian sanctions evasion networks adapted and yet 76 percent of the bank’s risk factor weights remained unchanged. Regulators also identified instances where inadequate risk factor weights were not appropriately recalibrated despite internal evidence of deficiencies.

An institution cannot continually update its understanding of financial crime risk if its professionals and leadership lack the geopolitical knowledge necessary to recognize how that risk is changing. What is needed is a fundamental restructuring of financial crime education in the private sector.

Year after year, the Association of Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialists, the professional association for financial crime professionals, identifies insufficient expertise and ongoing training as significant risks facing the private sector.

In its Global Anti-Financial Crime Threats Reports, 43 percent of surveyed professionals in 2024 , 50 percent in 2025 and 47 percent in 2026 considered insufficient skilled resources or ongoing training a high or very high risk to their financial crime functions.

Meanwhile, 63 percent of respondents in the 2026 report identified geopolitical instability as high or very high risk. The industry recognizes both the growing importance of geopolitically driven threats and persistent weaknesses in the expertise required to confront them.

Professionals must be taught how American national security, foreign policy and geopolitics force adaptation in their anti-financial crime programs, and how these developments fundamentally shift the risks and suspicious activities institutions must prioritize.

Regulatory operational training is a necessity, but an institution cannot effectively meet its regulatory obligations without training its staff to a higher standard of education surrounding how the world of illicit finance exists beyond screening lists and transaction monitoring systems.

But to do this, companies must have leaders who understand these complex dynamics and approach them with the seriousness, resources and ongoing training necessary to turn a static system into the dynamic one needed in a rapidly shifting risk environment.

Are financial institutions training their employees to simply work, or are they training them to truly think?

The financial sector does not simply need better operational compliance training. It needs to fundamentally reexamine its approach to how financial crime education is taught and, perhaps even more importantly, maintained in the modern world.

Because at the core, financial crime is not merely a compliance hurdle, but a problem that affects the safety of Americans and others around the world. And companies cannot effectively counter threats that their staff is fundamentally untrained to combat.

Brett Erickson is managing principal at Obsidian Risk Advisors and an advisory board member at Seton Hall School of Diplomacy and International Relations and DePaul University Driehaus College of Business.

articles.title: Precio de la luz por horas mañana, miércoles 21 de octubre: cuándo es más barata y más cara
articles.standfirst: Precio de la luz se abarata un 24,83% este miércoles
articles.summary: Precio de la luz se abarata un 24,83% este miércoles
articles.body: El precio medio de la electricidad hoy, 146,97 €/MWh, muestra una notable disminución de 48,55 € respecto al día anterior, cuando se situó en 195,52 €/MWh. Este miércoles, los consumidores pueden beneficiarse de estos precios más bajos. A medida que avanza el día, es relevante identificar las horas más costosas y las más económicas para optimizar el consumo. Los precios de la luz alcanzan su punto más alto durante las horas de mayor demanda, especialmente a partir de la mañana y hasta la noche. Durante el día, las franjas horarias más relevantes son, concretamente, entre las 07:00 - 08:00 (226.09 €/MWh) y 20:00 - 21:00 (284.49 €/MWh), donde se concentran los valores máximos. Esta tendencia se mantiene con picos significativos en 21:00 - 22:00 (284.93 €/MWh) y 19:00 - 20:00 (255.14 €/MWh). El bloque de horas caras es notable entre 07:00 y 22:00, con valores que superan considerablemente los 200 €/MWh, lo que refleja la variación de precios en función de la demanda eléctrica. La luz es más barata durante las primeras horas del día y al mediodía, ofreciendo oportunidades significativas de ahorro. Con tarifas que alcanzan precios muy bajos, como 0.75 €/MWh y 0.95 €/MWh entre las 13:00 - 15:00 y un momento crítico a las 11:00 - 12:00 con 1.99 €/MWh, existe una ventana amplia de precios bajos en la que los consumidores pueden beneficiarse. Las franjas horarias más relevantes que destacan en este análisis son 11:00 - 12:00, 12:00 - 13:00, 13:00 - 14:00 y 14:00 - 15:00, sumando hasta cuatro horas consecutivas de ahorro considerable. La jornada destaca por una considerable fluctuación en los precios, con un notable incremento de tarifas en las horas centrales, lo que refleja la volatilidad y el impacto de la demanda en el costo de la electricidad. Este patrón puede ser clave para los consumidores al planificar su consumo energético y optimizar sus gastos.

articles.title: United Airlines CEO calls for wealth tax
articles.summary: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby backed national wealth and inheritance taxes in an interview published Sunday, arguing they would help level the playing field for Americans. Kirby told The New York Times that wealth inequality “has become a danger to our society,” adding the federal government must “address” it. “We should have a national wealth…
articles.body:
United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby backed national wealth and inheritance taxes in an interview published Sunday, arguing they would help level the playing field for Americans.

Kirby told The New York Times that wealth inequality “has become a danger to our society,” adding the federal government must “address” it.

“We should have a national wealth tax — it won’t work by state because people will just move,” the United CEO added. “And I think we should have inheritance taxes that get close to 100 percent at some level. I would pay them.”

Progressive lawmakers and candidates have for years proposed a wealth tax to address income inequality and boost funding for social programs.

In California this midterm season, voters will decide whether the state will impose a one-time 5 percent tax on billionaires’ wealth. Revenue from the tax would fund state healthcare and food assistance programs, along with public education.

Forty-five percent of respondents to a poll the University of California Berkeley’s Institute of Governmental Studies conducted last month backed Proposition 40, which proposes the wealth tax. That is below the majority support needed for passage.

Forty-two percent of respondents were against the measure, while 13 percent were undecided.

Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) introduced legislation in March to establish a 5 percent annual wealth tax on households with a net worth of more than $1 billion.

The proposal would raise roughly $4.4 trillion over the next decade and cut the wealth of the “typical” billionaire in half after 15 years, according to an analysis from economists Emmanuel Saez and Gabriel Zuchman.

Another analysis researchers at the Tax Policy Center conducted last year found that a 1 percent wealth tax on households with greater than $50 million in assets — and greater than $25 million for unmarried filers — would raise nearly $2 trillion over a 10-year period.

articles.title: Farmers to get one-time payments from $8 billion program, Trump says: What to know
articles.summary: President Trump on Monday announced a program meant to give farmers one-time payments to help “offset diesel costs” this harvest season, but it likely won’t have an immediate impact.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – Farmers could soon receive one-time payments as part of an $8 billion program announced by President Donald Trump on Monday.

During a rally in Kansas, Trump unveiled the Harvest Fuel Relief Program, which he said is intended to “offset diesel costs during the harvest season.”

It comes at a time when diesel, in particular, has been especially high.

“Farmers and ranchers welcome the administration’s announcement of $8 billion in relief through the Harvest Fuel Relief program to help farmers struggling with high diesel prices,” American Farm Bureau Federation President Zippy Duvall said in a news release . “We appreciate President Trump and [U.S. Department of Agriculture] Secretary [Brooke] Rollins recognizing that higher diesel prices have squeezed farmers’ bottom lines.”

The USDA projects that net farm income will decline by 2.6% this year as production expenses rise by 4.5%. Fuel and oil expenses alone are expected to jump nearly 30%, according to the agency’s September forecast.

Payments from the program, however, likely won’t provide immediate relief. Here’s what to know.

What is the Harvest Fuel Relief Program?

The program is meant to “provide relief during temporary market disruptions and increased input costs,” a press release from the USDA explains .

In short, it is expected to disburse $8 billion worth of one-time payments to farmers “to cover a portion of modeled losses during the 2026 crop year.”

How will one-time payments be calculated?

The USDA said it will use a formula to determine how much each farmer receives, focused on modeled losses.

“This national loss average will be based on [Farm Service Agency] reported planted acres, Economic Research Service cost of production estimates, and World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates yields and prices,” the USDA explained.

Next month, commodity-specific payment rates for Title I commodities – common row crops like wheat, corn, soybeans, oats, peanuts, and more – are expected to be released. Methodology for payments related to other eligible commodities will come sometime after, the USDA said.

Those who deal with non-Title I commodities, like “specialty crop growers and fishermen,” are invited to “provide data related to increased fuel costs” via email for consideration when the USDA is determining pay rates.

Farmers do not need crop insurance linkage to qualify for the Harvest Fuel Relief program, but the USDA urges them to take advantage of it.

How and when can farmers get a one-time payment?

It likely won’t be until after the current harvest season that payments are sent out.

Payment amounts for row crops aren’t expected to be announced until November, “with details for other eligible commodities to follow,” per the USDA .

Applications will be available online via Login.gov , where pre-filled forms will also be made available, but not until January 2027. While those applications are not currently available, the USDA is encouraging farmers who believe they may qualify to create an account on Login.gov , if they haven’t already.

The Farm Service Agency, or FSA, is tasked with administering the payments, which the Trump administration said are authorized under the Commodity Credit Corporation.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Meta's Muse AI agent hits 10.9 million downloads as ChatGPT slides 25%
articles.summary: Muse downloads continue to move in the right direction for Meta.
articles.body:
If the excitement around Meta's ( META ) new Muse AI agent is slowing down, you certainly don't see it in the download numbers Wall Street is tracking like a hawk.

Meta's Muse has amassed 10.9 million downloads since its launch on Sept. 8, according to newly released data from Sensor Tower. Muse has received more than 10.2 million downloads from the US alone. In contrast, US downloads for OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) ChatGPT in the past 30 days have declined by 25% over the prior 30-day period.

Sensor Tower estimated that Muse reached 2.5 million daily active users (DAUs) for the first time on Oct. 16, as DAUs increased 15% week over week for the past seven days.

Only 11 other apps have reached 10 million US downloads within 40 days, Sensor Tower said, with the most recent app achieving this status being Meta's Threads in July 2023.

The momentum is likely welcome news to Wall Street, which has come out with aggressive growth assumptions for Muse since its release.

Deutsche Bank analyst Benjamin Black sees Muse reaching up to 8% of Meta's revenue by 2030, which nets out to roughly $36 billion in sales for the product. On the lower end of the prediction scale, Black sees Muse pulling in sales of $2.4 billion by 2030.

"In our view, Meta found a clear gap amongst current AI-agentic offerings — at the intersection of mobile app-based ecosystem, with a consumer-oriented UI which is seamless to use, the ability to complete transactions autonomously, free-to-use for the most part, and always-on feature within its own virtual machine — that makes it the service virtually unique in today's market," Black said.

Meta is slated to report earnings after the close of trading on Wednesday.

articles.title: Chip stocks shrug off a scary morning, but history says the shakeout isn't over
articles.summary: Chip stocks were in free fall at Tuesday's market open. By midmorning, they were leading a comeback.
articles.body:
Wall Street's AI darlings were in free fall at the open. By midmorning, they were leading the comeback.

The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) sank to its lowest level since early August early Tuesday. It was supposed to be the moment Monday's relief rally fell apart after an eight-session losing streak.

Instead, buyers stormed in. The index is now higher on the day and back above Friday's close, springing a bear trap much like the one forming in CoreWeave ( CRWV ).

The rebound is broad too. Roughly 3 of every 4 stocks in a 60-stock Yahoo Finance chip basket have turned green, including heavyweights AMD ( AMD ), Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ), Intel ( INTC ), and Micron ( MU ). GlobalFoundries ( GFS ) tops the list.

Notice who's missing from the party. Chip equipment makers Lam Research ( LRCX ), KLA ( KLAC ), and Applied Materials ( AMAT ) are still in the red, along with Arm ( ARM ). Even Nvidia ( NVDA ), the AI trade's bellwether, is barely keeping up.

Buyers are picking their spots, favoring the companies that make chips over the ones that sell them the tools.

History says the real test may still be ahead

The track record says don't count on the bottom being in just yet.

After every losing streak of seven sessions or more since 1994, the index traded below the streak's final close within a month, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. After the longest streaks, it was lower a month later most of the time.

And those dips weren't shallow. The typical one after the longest streaks ran about 9%. Tuesday's barely scratched 1% before buyers pounced.

One-day comebacks like this one haven't settled the question either. They've been a coin flip for chips.

The bulls do get a consolation prize. Three months out, the index was usually higher.

BofA Global Research called last week's rout a "positioning-driven hiccup on the fringes of the AI trade" in a research report. If that's right, the bounce has room to run. If not, the next dip is the one to watch.

For the index, it starts with the summer floor around 11,000 to 11,140, built from lows in late July and September, plus Friday's close. Holding it keeps Tuesday's comeback intact.

Lose it, and the next stop is the 10,450 to 10,500 zone, where chips bottomed in late July and traded in late April.

On the upside, bulls first need to clear 12,600 to 12,700, which capped the index in early October. Above that sits the early-October peak zone near 13,200 to 13,350.

Watch whether Tuesday's low holds and that big 11,000 level just underneath. That's where the silicon meets the road.

articles.title: Newsprint makers seek PM's intrevention over coal supply disruptions

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian Newsprint Manufacturers’ Association (INMA) has sought Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s intervention to address persistent coal supply disruptions, alleging irregular dispatches of coal rakes by Coal India Ltd subsidiaries despite valid fuel supply agreements (FSAs).In a representation to the PM, the association said newsprint manufacturers were facing production constraints due to coal shortages, forcing them to procure the fuel from the open market and rely on grid power at high costs to keep their mills running.INMA, which represents domestic newsprint manufacturers supplying major print media houses, including The Times of India, Hindustan Times, The Hindu and Punjab Kesari, said delays in coal dispatches, followed by sudden bunching of rakes, were creating operational, logistical, storage and financial challenges for mills.The association also flagged the diversion of coal supplies towards the power sector, claiming that more than 95% of total coal supplies were currently being allocated to power producers, leaving non-regulated sector industries, including newsprint manufacturers, struggling to secure adequate supplies. It urged govt to enforce the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs-recommended 75:25 coal allocation ratio between the power and non-power sectors to ensure adequate supplies to manufacturing industries.Seeking immediate corrective measures, INMA asked the PMO to direct CIL and its subsidiaries, including Northern Coalfields Ltd, Central Coalfields Ltd, South Eastern Coalfields Ltd and Western Coalfields Ltd, to ensure timely, regular and evenly spaced dispatches of coal rakes in line with existing FSAs.The association warned that continued shortages could force domestic newsprint manufacturers to cut production, disrupting supplies of a key raw material to newspapers and putting financial pressure on the print media industry. articles.title: Indian Railways’ train reaches Chhattisgarh’s Rowghat for the first time since Independence with Tadoki-Rowghat railway line; remote area finally gets connected to national rail network
articles.summary: Indian Railways has taken another major step towards improving rail connectivity with Rowghat in Chhattisgarh being connected by trains for the first time
articles.body: Indian Railways has taken another major step towards improving rail connectivity with Rowghat in Chhattisgarh being connected by trains for the first time since Independence. The Tadoki-Rowghat and Abhanpur-Kurud broad-gauge railway lines were inaugurated on Tuesday. The event was attended by Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai, while Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw joined through video conferencing.Two new passenger train services, Rowghat-Raipur and Raipur-Kurud, were also flagged off during the programme. The foundation stone for an electric locomotive maintenance facility in Raipur was laid on the occasion.Chhattisgarh’s Rowghat finally on rail mapThe arrival of a train in Rowghat for the first time since independence is a landmark development for southern Chhattisgarh, bringing its remote areas closer to the national railway network. The newly inaugurated lines and passenger services are expected to improve regional connectivity and give residents better travel options.Addressing the gathering, Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai said development work across Chhattisgarh, including in the railway sector, had been progressing steadily. The state has received an allocation of more than Rs 7,000 crore under this year's Railway Budget, he noted.Sai expressed confidence that the projects would bring better rail services to the state's remote regions and give an additional push to industrial activity, trade and wider socio-economic development.Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw also congratulated the people of Chhattisgarh on the completion of these important railway projects and the introduction of the new Rowghat-Raipur and Raipur-Kurud passenger train services.He said railway infrastructure in Chhattisgarh was being expanded steadily. Several important projects have already been completed, including the Dalli-Rajhara-Rowghat railway line, gauge conversion of the Kendi-Abhanpur-Rajim-Dhamtari section and multiple projects to add railway tracks.Construction is also in progress on the Kharsia-Parmalkasa double-line project. In addition, the Cabinet has recently approved a third railway line between Pendra Road, Bilaspur and Uslapur. These initiatives are expected to improve rail connectivity across Chhattisgarh, upgrade passenger facilities and support industrial and economic expansion.The 95-km railway line connecting Dalli-Rajhara and Rowghat has been completed at a cost of Rs 1,628 crore. The project reached completion with the finishing of the 17.5-km stretch between Tadoki and Rowghat.With Rowghat now connected by rail, residents of the remote region will have easier access to transport, helping them reach educational institutions, healthcare facilities, employment opportunities and markets.The new railway link is also expected to stimulate industrial and economic activity in the area. It will particularly facilitate faster transportation of iron ore from the Rowghat region, helping meet the requirements of India's iron and steel industry, including the Bhilai Steel Plant.Better rail access will make it easier to move raw materials and support the growth of industries. The project is also expected to open up fresh employment opportunities and encourage economic activity in the region.Under the gauge conversion programme covering the Kendri-Dhamtari and Abhanpur-Rajim sections, passenger train operations have already begun between Abhanpur and Rajim. Separately, the 22-km Abhanpur-Kurud stretch has been converted to broad gauge as part of the Abhanpur-Dhamtari project.Work on the remaining section between Kurud and Dhamtari is continuing and is expected to be completed shortly.The opening of the Abhanpur-Kurud broad-gauge line has further extended railway connectivity in the region. Passengers will have improved travel options to Raipur, the state capital, while the new link is also expected to support local trade, regional development and everyday commuting.The newly introduced passenger services on the Rowghat-Raipur and Raipur-Kurud routes will give residents of these areas direct rail access to Raipur, making travel more convenient.You use AI every day. articles.title: Tesla Q3 preview: Delivery outlook, cash flow, and a dash of merger speculation on tap
articles.summary: Tesla will report third quarter results after the closing bell on Wednesday, with profits and cash flow squarely in focus along with a dash of merger specula...
articles.body:
Tesla ( TSLA ) will report third quarter results after the closing bell on Wednesday, with profits and cash flow squarely in focus, with a dash of merger speculation.

Tesla is expected to report Q3 revenue of $28.13 billion, flat year over year, per Bloomberg consensus. Adjusted EPS is estimated at $0.44, with adjusted EBITDA of $3.66 billion.

Consensus EBIT of $760 million, a 2.7% margin, would be a step up from $400 million and 1.4% in Q2.

Tesla stock is still down about 17% this year, a test for investors, but typically the company rallies on stronger deliveries in the back half of the year.

Tesla reported Q3 deliveries of 486,532, down 2% from a year ago but well ahead of Bloomberg consensus of 463,000. Energy storage deployments came in at 13.7 GWh, up from 12.5 GWh a year ago and Q2's 13.5 GWh.

Tesla's sales in its key territories are moving in different directions. The US is still feeling the loss of the $7,500 federal EV tax credit, which set off a buying rush in last year's third quarter before it expired. Cox Automotive estimates Tesla sold around 144.1K EVs in the US in Q3, down nearly 20% year over year. That was still about 54% of the US EV market, more than all other brands combined.

Tesla's Shanghai, however, posted a September wholesale volume of 95,366 vehicles, its best month of 2026, with exports up 58%, while domestic sales fell 9%. In Europe, Tesla registrations across the EU, UK, and EFTA rose 43.3% from January through August, per ACEA .

Free cash flow (FCF) is again the number to watch, and it's expected to be deeply negative. Per Tesla's own sell-side analyst consensus , Wall Street sees Q3 FCF at -$4.51 billion, with capital expenditures climbing to $7.77 billion for the quarter. A year ago, FCF was nearly $4 billion.

Tesla has guided to more than $25 billion in capex for 2026, vs. roughly $8.5 billion spent last year. The money is going to Optimus production lines, AI compute, the Cybercab ramp, and the Terafab chip plant it is building with SpaceX.

Elon Musk made clear over the weekend where he thinks that spending pays off. "Optimus and Cybercab will be the vast majority of Tesla's value," Tesla's CEO posted on X on Saturday.

Tesla began commercial Cybercab service in Austin on Sept. 3, but federal regulators have questions. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) issued Tesla a special order with 21 requests on how it self-certified the Cybercab, which has no steering wheel or pedals, as compliant with federal safety standards. Tesla asked for an extension to Nov. 20. NHTSA granted 30 days instead , making answers due Oct. 30.

Benchmark international contract Brent North Sea crude and its US counterpart WTI both briefly climbed above $110 per barrel.

Asian equity markets ended the day with losses.

"Last night's tech recovery on Wall Street didn't carry over into Asian markets with AI-related names in the region facing renewed pressure on their share prices," said AJ Bell investment director Russ Mould

Seoul and Tokyo again bore the brunt of the selling as chip giants SK hynix, Samsung and Kioxia took another beating owing to a sharp exit from a sector that saw blistering gains in the first half of this year.

South Korea's Kospi stocks index sank nearly four percent, with SK hynix off 4.2 percent and Samsung down three percent.

Further weighing on sentiment was the data centre infrastructure firm Elice, whose shares collapsed more than 30 percent on their trading debut.

The negative sentiment carried over to equity trading in Europe.

The euro rose against the dollar but remained under pressure as violent cost-of-living protests in France and Italy have pushed up government bond yields.

The yield on France's 10-year government bond rose to 4.94 percent Tuesday, more than 150 basis points above the comparable German government bond, considered the European benchmark of creditworthiness.

The resulting spread between the two yields is the highest since the closing levels of January 2012, when the eurozone was in the midst of a credit crisis that required market interventions by the European Central Bank to keep borrowing costs from spiralling.

Wall Street managed to clamber into positive territory on Tuesday despite continued volatility in artificial intelligence shares as investors digested mixed earnings from industrial companies.

articles.title: Macron lines up more Gulf diesel as France battles soaring fuel prices
articles.summary: The UAE and Bahrain deals increase French commitments to 295,000 tonnes a month, just over 10 percent of consumption.
articles.body:
French President Emmanuel Macron has secured commitments for an extra 200,000 tonnes of diesel a month from the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, according to the French presidency.

The Elysee Palace announced the deals on Tuesday, before the president landed in Qatar.

His three-day Gulf tour, which also stops in Kuwait, follows a weekend of violent protests in France over the soaring cost of living, as the US-Iran war keeps energy prices high.

The presidency said the UAE had committed to about 100,000 tonnes a month, while a further 100,000 tonnes monthly would be secured during Macron’s visit to Bahrain .

Together with deliveries from Saudi Arabia, France now has commitments for 295,000 tonnes a month, just over 10 percent of its consumption, it said.

Kuwait has also given “very clear commitments” to deliver diesel and kerosene to the French overseas territories of Mayotte and Reunion in the Indian Ocean, the presidency said. The shipments will go via Oman to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

Patrick Pouyanne, the head of French oil giant TotalEnergies, who is travelling with Macron, said the deals would “reassure the French”.

“We are not going to run out of diesel in February,” he said, according to the AFP news agency.

Andreas Krieg, a professor at the School of Security Studies at King’s College London, told Al Jazeera that France’s energy deals fit a wider pattern.

He noted that Gulf states have sent delegations to London, Paris, Berlin and Rome in recent months, seeking access to military complexes and possible stakes in European defence companies.

“They see a growing entanglement between their interests and European interests,” he said. “Not just in the energy field,” but also supply chains, he added.

Both sides feel pressure from a United States that is increasingly sidelining them, creating an opening to minimise dependence on Washington, Krieg said.

Macron’s agenda in Qatar includes discussions about security, defence, securing energy commitments to France, and advancing the frontiers in artificial intelligence, according to Sheikha Alanoud Hamad Saud Al Thani, a political analyst and fellow at the Middle East Council for Global Affairs.

Speaking to Al Jazeera, she said Qatar “really valued” its ties with France, which is one of the Gulf state’s oldest defence relationships.

“It comes as no surprise that the French are one of Qatar’s most important friends in Europe,” she said, describing Macron’s visit as “extremely consequential”.

“[Qatar is] leveraging existing relationships to adapt to this new kind of asymmetrical warfare, and we’re looking to see advancements in anti-drone and defence capabilities,” she said.

Iran has blockaded the Strait of Hormuz, the main exit route for the Gulf’s energy exports, sending crude prices soaring during the eight-month conflict. Diesel has been among the hardest hit.

The G7, chaired this year by France, agreed earlier in October to draw up to 100 million barrels of oil from strategic reserves.

France has also released 10 million barrels of diesel from its own reserves, aiming to cut prices by 12 to 18 cents a litre, or about 5 to 8 percent, from next month, the French presidency said.

articles.title: The Villages is betting $180M on more retirees moving to Florida — where home sales are stale
articles.summary: The Villages, the largest retirement community in the US, plans to issue $180 million in high-yield debt to finance more homebuilding.
articles.body:
The Villages, the largest retirement community in the US with roughly 170,000 residents across 57,000 acres in central Florida, is aiming to get even bigger.

The resort-like community plans to issue $180 million in high-yield debt primarily to finance more homes, according to an investor presentation this week.

The proceeds of the upcoming bond offering will fund construction of 3,860 new residential units and additional golf courses and recreation centers, according to Bloomberg .

The community is already massive, with more than 50 golf courses, 100-plus swimming pools, and several town squares, and its latest expansion bets big on luring droves of more boomers and Gen Xers to the Sunshine State.

But it's happening as the bond market is under duress , with even the mighty US Treasury market competing for investors. The housing market is grounded by high mortgage rates and high home prices. Florida has been hit particularly hard by the trends. Sales of existing single-family homes there were down 3.5% in September from a year ago, according to the Florida Realtors Association. And net migration into the state slowed sharply last year compared to the pandemic boom years.

What's more: The notion of what makes an ideal retirement community is evolving.

"The retirement relocation conversation in this country has been dominated by weather, taxes, and cost of living for decades," demographic strategist Bradley Schurman told Yahoo Finance. "Those are real factors, but they tell you almost nothing about whether a place will remain livable and financially viable over the 25 years that matter most to a new retiree."

The Villages taps into several essential keys to healthy aging — community and social engagement, along with a focus on fitness and recreation.

Its expansion plans would have around 260,000 people living there with more than 130,000 homes by 2045.

So far this year, more than 2,100 homes in the Villages have sold for an average of just under $500,000, per Bloomberg.

"There's still juice in these master planned communities like the Villages, and there's a market for them," Schurman said.

But while the Villages has been a colossal draw for retirees seeking warm weather, low taxes, and a low cost of living, more factors related to affordability and sustainability have entered the conversation.

An index released earlier this year ranked communities on climate resilience, automation readiness, social cohesion, population renewal, and governance and foresight. For example, if an area's population is stable or growing, basic government services are more likely to be funded.

articles.summary: By Anushree Mukherjee Oct 20 (Reuters) - Gold edged lower on Tuesday as investors weighed the likelihood of additional US interest rate hikes this year ahead...
articles.body:
Oct 20 (Reuters) - Gold edged lower on Tuesday as investors weighed the likelihood of additional US interest rate hikes this year ahead ‌of next week's Federal Reserve policy meeting.

Spot gold was down 0.3% at $4,125.90 per ‌ounce by 02:05 p.m. EDT (1805 GMT). US gold futures for December delivery settled 0.4% lower at $4,142.60 per ​ounce.

"Inflation and the Fed's interest rates are the big stories that gold's fighting at the moment. US Treasuries do appear more favorable than gold as a safety asset for the moment," said Bob Haberkorn, senior market strategist at StoneX.

"$4,000 is a big level for (gold) to ‌keep an eye on and ⁠see if it can hold. A lot of that, at the moment, is going to be dependent on what the Fed says," Haberkorn ⁠said.

The Fed raised interest rates by a quarter point in September, its first hike this year.

While recent comments from Fed officials signaling little urgency for further policy tightening have tempered ​expectations of ​a rate hike at the central bank's ​October 27-28 policy meeting, traders see ‌a 92% chance of a hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool. [FEDWATCH]

Gold is still down about 26% from its record high of $5,594.82 in January and roughly 22% from levels at the start of the Iran war, when concerns over energy inflation reinforced bets on interest rate hikes.

Gold is traditionally seen as an inflation hedge, but it loses ‌its appeal as a non-yielding asset in a high-interest-rate ​environment.

Investors are also watching next week's US Personal ​Consumption Expenditures (PCE) data, the Federal Reserve's ​preferred inflation gauge, for clues on whether inflation pressures remain persistent ‌and how that could shape the rate ​outlook.

In Japan, central bank ​Governor Kazuo Ueda said underlying inflation was "quite close" to the 2% target, signaling scope for further rate hikes.

Among other metals, spot silver rose 1.4% to $57.86 per ​ounce, platinum gained 1% ‌to $1,656.85 per ounce and palladium dropped 1.3% to $1,105.50 per ounce.

articles.title: Spotify says it removed 50 million ‘slop’ and spam AI tracks this year
articles.summary: Spotify removed more than 50 million tracks created by AI so far this year, as it works to keep AI-generated music from crowding out human artists.
articles.body: Spotify has removed more than 50 million tracks that appear to have been created by artificial intelligence from its curated music recommendations so far this year, as the streaming giant works to keep AI-generated music from crowding out human artists. “AI-generated slop and spam don’t belong in your recommendations, and we’ve made changes to keep them out and protect the listening experience,” Spotify said in a statement Tuesday. Last year, the company removed 75 million tracks for what it said were serious or repeated violations of its rules, which prohibit replicating an existing creator’s content or creating media artificially with technology. The flood of AI-generated creative content online poses a major challenge to streaming services like Spotify, which need to identify and weed out instances of impersonation or deception from among tens of millions of tracks. Here, Spotify said it turned to its listeners for help. The company analyzed patterns within songs that users frequently skipped or ignored on the platform over the past six months. These tracks consistently overlapped with the artificially generated audio sometimes referred to as “slop.” By combining feedback from listeners with metadata and third-party AI-detection tools, Spotify was able to update its internal recommendation system to limit how often AI-generated content was surfaced. The company acknowledged that AI-detection technology has limitations and that identifying suspicious content could become more difficult as generative AI evolves. For Spotify, the presence of AI-generated music can also have huge implications for artists who are paid based, in part, on how often their music is played relative to the total number of streams on the platform. “If the denominator has grown because of AI slop, the percentage that each legitimate rights holder or artist will receive is diminished,” said Morgan Hayduk, CEO of Beatdapp, which sells AI- and fraud-detection software to music labels and distributors. To be eligible for royalties on Spotify, an artist must reach a minimum of 1,000 streams, which is far less common for AI tracks than it is for human-made music. But not all artists who use AI in their creative process publish what Spotify may consider “slop.” For these situations, Spotify launched an AI credits feature earlier this year that artists can use to disclose which parts of a song’s creative process involved AI. The combined use of audience feedback, metadata and detection tools to identify AI slop is one of several features that Spotify has introduced this year to increase transparency around AI use on the platform. It also labels the artist profiles of musicians it believes are AI-generated with an “AI Persona” badge. AI Persona artists are excluded from user recommendation streams by default. Only listeners who proactively follow a particular AI artist will see that persona recommended to them. Spotify said these efforts have resulted in a “marked decrease” in the number of concerns from listeners about AI spam showing up in their recommendations. “AI moves fast and bad actors adapt just as fast,” Spotify said. “But as AI makes music more abundant, we believe listeners will value human artistry even more.”

articles.title: Meta Q3 earnings to test Wall Street's stomach for AI spending
articles.summary: Meta will report its third quarter earnings after the bell on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Meta ( META ) will kick off Big Tech's earnings season when it reports its third quarter results after the bell on Wednesday.

For the third quarter, Meta is expected to post earnings per share of $3.56 on revenue of $63.3 billion, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus estimates. That's up from the $1.05 and $51.2 billion the company reported in Q3 last year.

Capital expenditures, however, are projected to increase 117% year over year to $41 billion. Meta's Reality Labs segment is expected to see an operating loss of $5.2 billion.

The company's earnings come as AI investors waver between hope and concern over CoreWeave's ( CRWV ) debt load.

Adding to the unease is a report from Gartner last week stating that AI revenue infrastructure firms are set to spend upwards of $8.5 trillion through 2030, but that consumer and enterprise AI revenue will total just $3.6 trillion, potentially leaving "more than $4 trillion in asset value exposed to write-down risk through 2032."

Meta stock is down more than 3% over the last year, as Wall Street has sought more clarity on how the company plans to monetize its prodigious spending.

But the social media giant has also had several wins in recent weeks. Its Muse AI agent reached 10 million downloads just 40 days after its US launch, market intelligence firm Sensor Tower announced Tuesday.

That's faster than OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) ChatGPT and Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) Claude, which hit the mark in 123 days and 673 days, respectively.

Meta also debuted its frontier-class Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full AI models , proving it can compete with the likes of Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic.

And last month, CEO Mark Zuckerberg debuted a number of new hardware products at the company's Meta Connect conference , including the latest Ray-Ban Meta glasses, the audio-only Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses, and the upcoming $1,299 Meta VR Glasses.

"Recent AI launches have strengthened confidence in the company's AI execution, and we see Meta with the least risk of AI disruption to its core business in our coverage," BofA Global Research analyst Justin Post wrote in a note to investors ahead of the company's earnings.

articles.title: Trump launches $25 million whistleblower incentive program; Nick Shirley receives first payout
articles.summary: President Trump and Vice President Vance announced a $25 million whistleblower program that would pay out cash for people who tip off the federal government about fraudsters. The Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program will offer a 1 percent commission to those who provide a tip that leads to a successful conviction. The president said he will…
articles.body:
President Trump and Vice President Vance announced a $25 million whistleblower program that would pay out cash for people who tip off the federal government about fraudsters.

The Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program will offer a 1 percent commission to those who provide a tip that leads to a successful conviction. The president said he will act as the sole arbitrator of who receives payouts.

“If anybody turns anybody in… you get a 1 percent commission, and I think that will be amazing, because the kind of money that’s been stolen is trillions from this country,” Trump said in the Oval Office.

Anyone can submit a tip through fraud.gov, Trump said. He said he will act as “binding” arbitrator if there are multiple claims to the same award, to “expedite” the process.

“In other words, I’ll determine whether or not the person is deserving…and I will be very generous,” he said.

The first award was apparently given to conservative YouTuber Nick Shirley, who joined Trump and Vance in the Oval Office. Fox News reported that Shirley would receive $10,000.

Shirley became a viral sensation on the right last year after posting a video documenting his search for fraudulent childcare programs in Minnesota.

The whistleblower program builds on the work of Vance’s anti-fraud task force.

“The president has said it must stop,” Vance said of fraud. “It is stopping, and if you want to help us stop it, you get to share in the rewards now, thanks to what the president of the United States has done.”

Trump created the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud in March, with Vance as chairman. The force was created to look into and reduce fraud in federal government programs.

articles.title: El Gobierno blinda ante los sindicatos la subida del 4,5% a los funcionarios en 2027 pese al adelanto electoral
articles.standfirst: La medida beneficiaría a más de tres millones de empleados públicos
articles.summary: La medida beneficiaría a más de tres millones de empleados públicos
articles.body: El Gobierno de España ha garantizado al 100% a los sindicatos que cumplirá con la subida salarial del 4,5% para los funcionarios en el próximo año 2027, blindando este compromiso a pesar de la convocatoria de elecciones generales anticipadas programadas para el próximo 29 de noviembre. En la reunión de la Comisión de Seguimiento celebrada este martes entre el Ministerio para la Transformación Digital y de la Función Pública y los sindicatos CSIF, CCOO y UGT, el Ejecutivo ratificó su intención de aplicar los términos recogidos en el acuerdo marco firmado a finales de 2025. Con esta subida, que beneficia a más de tres millones de empleados públicos, se busca asegurar la estabilidad de las retribuciones del sector con independencia del resultado electoral. Aunque el incremento para el 2027 está asegurado políticamente, el Ejecutivo no ha especificado exactamente cuándo se aprobará la norma legal para hacerlo efectivo. Esto ha generado exigencias inmediatas por parte de los representantes de los trabajadores. CCOO exige que la subida se apruebe formalmente mediante un Real Decreto-ley para que pueda entrar en vigor el mismo día 1 de enero de 2027. Por su parte, UGT y CSIF reclaman que la aprobación en el Consejo de Ministros se realice antes del 24 de noviembre (la última cita antes de las elecciones generales del 29-N) para evitar que el cambio de Gobierno bloquee o retrase el proceso. Además del plano salarial, en la reunión del comité de seguimiento se trataron otros aspectos normativos pendientes de desarrollo como el abuso de la temporalidad (se busca endurecer las sanciones a las administraciones que incumplan los límites de interinidad) o los complementos geográficos (los sindicatos insisten en acelerar la revisión de los complementos de residencia e insularidad).
